Track A fp_zexp: ALL 69.752/7.201, neutral 1104.7, N<=10 1.709, 11-36 15.40, N>=37 146.99. fp_dft (207 rows): 1.319/0.726, neutral 3.303 (MAE 0.289 eV; the summary says 0.28), Z<=18 0.803, H-like 1.363. fp_dft_ts: 1.157, neutral 3.00. fp_zexp_univ in-sample: 38.72/4.10, neutral 819. fp_bohr: 1340.3, neutral 22527. He-like: zexp 0.29 -> zexp3_lit 0.217. Li-like: 0.689 -> 0.294. N/Z<=0.2 zexp2_rel: 0.48. Track B se_gshm: 1.573/0.737, neutral 7.612 (MAE 0.572 eV), 58.7% within 1%. se_gshm_core: 1.618/0.795, neutral 7.711. Baselines: se_slater_total 11.77/51.8, se_bohr 1362.9/22878, se_cr_1e 31.21/180.0.

HELD-OUT RE-RUN with my own script. For Track B I refitted on each training mask (fitlib.auto_tie + fitlib.fit), predicted through the public gshm.predict_many, and scored the test rows with evaluate.evaluate(subset=...). Results: final S1 1.587/0.728/neutral 6.70; S2 18.71/3.60/234.8; S3 1.700/0.801/8.12. Core S1 1.633/0.784/6.89; S2 19.23/1.53/259.8; S3 1.707/0.794/8.36. Each fit takes about 1-2 s. For Track A I re-ran zexp2nd.fit_univ on each training mask. 12-parameter universal sigma: S1 38.61/4.02/851, S2 65.32/4.31/1415, S3 42.90/4.57/789. Zero-parameter model: S1 68.34/7.00/1092, S2 77.79/7.42/1772, S3 74.25/8.34/1171. All match the claims.

LEAKAGE, Track B. gshm.predict() and configs.initial_final read only configurations (NIST ground-configuration table or Madelung); no IE_eV is read. IE_eV enters only through dataset()['y'], which is used as the fit target. fitlib.fit is called on ~test masks only. The ridge prior is Slater-like constants plus kappa0 = 7, not values fitted on data. There are 32 global parameters (18 sigma + 3 tau + kappa + 5 r_lj + 3 x_l + 2 b) and no per-element or per-ion parameters.

LEAKAGE, Track A. zexp.predict uses only exact rational coefficients, Dirac energies, and the external YS15 F_SE values and nuclear radii. It reads no NIST IE values. The per-key dE2 fit (366/78/343 parameters per split) and the 12-parameter universal fit are trained on ~test masks only. Both are labelled semi-empirical. zexp3_seq (409 parameters, in-sample) is labelled in-sample.

PREDICT CONSISTENCY. predict() matches the published CSVs on 40 random rows: max relative difference 2e-16 for Track A and 3e-8 for Track B. zexp2nd.pred_sq times Hartree equals fp_zexp_predictions to 6e-15, so the headline zexp model is zexp_sq_rel with p = 2.

OUT-OF-TABLE INPUTS. Track B works everywhere I tried: Og (118,118) = 6.59 eV, (120,2) = 261411 eV, (120,120) = 5.39 eV, (119,1) = 257599 eV. Track A works for (118,118) = 204.8 eV (useless; the literature value is about 8.9 eV), (112,112) and (120,118). It crashes with KeyError for (120,2), (119,1), (111,1) and (118,2); see issues.

PHYSICS SPOT CHECKS. config_energy gives E1(He 1s2) = 5/8 exactly. E1(Li 1s2 2s) = 5965/5832 = 1.0228052, which matches my hand value 5/8 + 2*17/81 - 16/729. He-like dE1 = -5/8 gives sigma1 = 5/8. Li-like dE1 = -0.397805 gives sigma1 = 1.59122. Na sigma1 = 7.786 and Cs sigma1 = 42.83, as the summary says. Dirac point-nucleus 1s binding at Z = 92 is 132279.934 eV, both mine (mc^2[1 - sqrt(1-(Z alpha)^2)]) and the code's. The full H-like layer for U gives 131819.13 eV vs NIST 131816.2 eV (22 ppm). HARTREE_EV / (2 RYDBERG_EV) = 1.000000 and 1/alpha = 137.035999, so there is no factor-of-2 problem. Slater's rules in baselines.slater_sigma give the textbook values: Zn 4s sigma = 25.65 (Zeff 4.35) and N 2p sigma = 3.10 (Zeff 3.90).

(a) DFT VALIDATION AUDIT. The reference is models/first_principles/cache/nist_dft_reference.json. It holds the NIST Atomic Reference Data for Electronic Structure Calculations (Kotochigova, Levine, Shirley, Stiles, Clark) in the LDA, LSD, RLDA and ScRLDA columns. The functional is the same one: Slater exchange + VWN correlation, spin-unpolarised for the LDA comparison and polarised for LSD. I re-ran the solver. He LDA = -2.8348356 (ref -2.834836, diff 4e-7, 1.8 s). Ne LDA = -128.2334813 (ref -128.233481, diff -3e-7). H LSD = -0.4786708 (ref -0.478671). These are all in Hartree; no Hartree/Rydberg or polarised/unpolarised mismatch. docs/first_principles.md line 204 says explicitly that this agreement 'only verifies the implementation, not physical accuracy'. Line 220 reports the physical error: Ne LDA -128.2335 vs exact -128.9376 Ha. The Delta-SCF IE errors against NIST are reported (3.3% for neutrals; H-like 1.4% from self-interaction). Three Delta-SCF rows recomputed: Na 5.3684, O 13.8965, Ne+ 41.5871 eV. All equal the CSV; NIST gives 5.139, 13.618, 40.963. Verdict: framed correctly.

(b) H-LIKE CIRCULARITY AUDIT. Track A's 1s/2s self-energy F_SE values, Uehling values, nuclear rms radii and M/m are all taken per Z from Yerokhin and Shabaev 2015 (JPCRD 44, 033103), in yerokhin_shabaev_2015_qed.json. Spot check: F_SE(1s, Z=1) = 10.316794, the standard value. The NIST H-like IEs in data/nist_ie.csv are all 'theoretical', and their uncertainties (U +-0.5 eV, Ds +-16 eV) look like YS15's. The CSV has no reference column, so I could not confirm the source from the data. The doc itself says NIST's H-like values come from YS15 theory. Therefore the 0.00117% (12 ppm) layer is consistency with the same theory, not independent validation, and the doc says so (line 166). The layers are reported as required and reproduce exactly: Dirac only 0.1902% (max 0.91%); + recoil + finite size 0.1134% (max 0.248%); + tabulated QED 0.00117% (max 0.0096%); closed-form Z-alpha self-energy 0.354%. The doc counts the 2x110 F_SE values and the radii as external theory or nuclear inputs, not fitted parameters (lines 145, 150, 352). The remaining residual (U: 2.9 eV over-binding) is consistent with the omitted two-loop QED and nuclear polarisation.

Track B's disclosures are accurate. The sigma_core bound was added after seeing S2 (doc line 273). The sparse-term choice used the S1 pool, which overlaps the S2 and S3 test sets (line 297). The S2 history (851 -> 391 -> 178.5 -> 19.2%) is in the doc table and in se_validation.json.

issues.title: Track A predict() crashes for Z > 110 whenever an s electron is removed
issues.evidence: zexp.predict(120,2), (119,1), (111,1) and (118,2) raise KeyError. relativity.F_SE / F_U index _QED[int(Z)], and the YS15 table stops at Z = 110. nuclear_params falls back for Z > 110, but qed_shift does not. Removing p, d or f electrons works ((118,118) and (120,118) return values). The brief requires predict(Z, N) to work for any (Z, N), and the orchestrator named (120,2) as a test case. Also, dirac_point gives NaN for 1s at Z >= 138 (Z alpha > 1).
issues.suggested_fix: In F_SE and F_U, return the Z = 110 value or a smooth extrapolation of the last few table points for Z > 110, and flag the result as extrapolated. Alternatively skip QED above 110 with a warning. Guard dirac_point for Z alpha >= |kappa|. Add a regression test for (120,2), (119,1) and (118,2).

issues.title: Track B's headline S2 number depends on a constraint chosen after seeing the S2 test set; the blind S2 result is 178.5% MAPE
issues.evidence: se_validation.json: core_S2_tied_ridge_only gives MAPE 178.50%, median 1.41%, neutral 7953%. That is the last variant built without looking at the S2 test set. Adding 0.8 <= sigma_core <= 1 afterwards gives 19.23%. The bound is disclosed (doc line 273), but the summary table and headline give 19.23 / 18.71 as 'S2 test MAPE'. The 'core' spec also contains core_bounds = [0.8, 1.0] and ridge 0.1. So the doc's statement that the core rows 'have no such issue' (line 297) is true only for term selection, not for the bound.
issues.suggested_fix: Report two S2 rows in every headline table: 'blind (pre-registered) 178.5% / median 1.41% / neutral 7953%' and 'with physics bound chosen post hoc 19.2%'. Reword 'core rows clean' to 'core rows free of term-selection leakage; the sigma_core bound is post hoc for S2'. In unification, fix the deep-core screening from Track A's exact sigma1 instead of a bound tuned on the test set. That is a legitimate prior-based fix that can be evaluated blind.

issues.title: Track B's sparse (Z alpha)^2 corrections hurt extrapolation in Z; the core model is the better extrapolator
issues.evidence: Reproduced S2 median: final 3.60% vs core 1.53%. The summary's 'S2 median 1.5%' refers to core, while the final model is the advertised headline. The terms were selected on the S1 training pool, which includes all Z >= 55 rows except multiples of 5.
issues.suggested_fix: For any claim about extrapolation, or as the base of the unified model, use GSHM core (30 parameters). Alternatively, redo term selection inside each split's training set.

issues.title: Track B's model structure was discovered on all 5847 rows (structural leakage)
issues.evidence: explore.py loads every record (including all S1/S2/S3 test rows) to discover the Za = q+1 denominator, the kappa form, the screening-class definitions and Za_mode. The held-out splits refit parameters only. They test parameter generalisation, not generalisation of the discovered functional form.
issues.suggested_fix: State this explicitly next to the held-out table. The S2 failure modes (f electrons, deep core) show the structure does not automatically extrapolate.

issues.title: Track B's 'key discovery' tau/(Za+kappa) is close to known isoelectronic-sequence formulas; the novelty is overstated
issues.evidence: doc lines 19 and 75 call it 'the single most important discovery'. Expanding sequence energies in the ionic charge zeta = q+1, with screening corrections in 1/(zeta + s), is classical: Edlén's isoelectronic-sequence formulas (Handbuch der Physik, 1964), and Layzer's 1/Z expansion rewritten in zeta. What is new is a single universal kappa shared across all sequences and classes in a global fit. That is a useful empirical finding, not a new law.
issues.suggested_fix: Cite Edlén (1964) and Layzer (1959). Present the result as 'a single universal Edlén-type denominator kappa = 8.2 works across all 110 sequences'.

issues.title: Track A's headline 'first principles, zero fitted parameters' formula contains heuristic modelling choices
issues.evidence: zexp = zexp_sq_rel with p = 2. Three choices are not exact: (i) the completed square adds dE2 ~ dE1^2/(4 dE0), which the doc says overestimates the true dE2 by about 25%; (ii) the relativistic correction is screened by ((Z - sigma1)/Z)^p with p = 2, and p = 4 is reported as slightly better on the data; (iii) QED for ns with n >= 3 uses F_SE(2s)/n^3 with the same screening factor. These are reasonable and partly disclosed (doc line 176; the summary says 'exact through O(Z)', which is correct). The formula is exact only through O(Z); everything beyond is modelling. On real atoms it is unusable: neutral first-IE MAPE is 1105%, and Og comes out at 204.8 eV against about 8.9 eV.
issues.suggested_fix: Label the headline as 'exact through O(Z) + heuristic O(1) completion; zero fitted parameters'. Keep 'first principles' for dE0, dE1 and the H-like layers. In the doc table, state that p = 2 was fixed a priori (Landé) before the p = 4 comparison.

issues.title: Three different 'Bohr' baselines
issues.evidence: fp_bohr 1340.3% (neutral 22527%), se_bohr 1362.9% (neutral 22878%), brief 1365%. They differ in how the removed-electron n and the rearranged rows are handled.
issues.suggested_fix: In the unified document, quote one Bohr baseline (se_bohr matches the brief's definition most closely) and footnote the other.

issues.title: Out-of-table extrapolation is unvalidated for superheavy elements
issues.evidence: Track B predicts Og (118,118) = 6.59 eV against relativistic coupled-cluster estimates of about 8.9 eV, roughly 26% low. It predicts E120 neutral = 5.39 eV against about 5.8 eV. That is in line with its 260% S2 neutral failure mode, though less severe. Track A gives 204.8 eV for Og.
issues.suggested_fix: Document predict() outside Z <= 110 as qualitative only. In the unified doc, compare against a few published superheavy IEs (Og, Fl, element 120) as a sanity check.

overall_verdict:
Both tracks are honest and reproducible. Every claimed metric, overall and held out, re-scores or re-fits to the printed precision. Neither predict() reads NIST IE values. There are no per-element or per-ion parameters, and every fit trains on ~test masks only.

Track A: the exact 1/Z coefficients (He 5/8, Li 5965/5832), the Dirac/QED layers and the LSDA solver are all verified. The DFT and H-like validation claims are framed correctly: implementation check against the same functional, and consistency with the same YS15 theory. Its weaknesses:
- One real code defect: predict() crashes for Z > 110 when an s electron is removed.
- The analytic formula is useless for near-neutral atoms (about 1100% error). Everything beyond O(Z) is heuristic.

Track B: GSHM (32 parameters, 1.57% MAPE, 1.59% S1, 1.70% S3) is the only usable closed formula. Its Z-extrapolation claim is weaker than the headline suggests:
- The blind S2 result is 178.5% MAPE.
- The 19.2% figure depends on a bound chosen after seeing the S2 test set (disclosed).
- The final model's sparse terms double the S2 median (1.5% to 3.6%).

No critical issues: no wrong results, no hidden leakage, no broken scoring.
notes_for_unification: Recommended base for the unified model: Track B GSHM core (30 parameters), not final. Core extrapolates better (S2 median 1.53% vs 3.60%), and final's sparse-term selection leaked across splits.

Fix S2 with physics instead of the post-hoc bound. Replace sigma_core and the f-class sigmas with Track A's exact first-order sigma1 values (zexp.coeffs(Z,N)['sigma'], or per-class decompositions), or use them as ridge priors. Then re-run S2 blind and report it against the blind 178.5% baseline, not against 19.2%.
For N = 1, use Track A's hlike layer (c) (0.00117%). Report it as consistency with YS15 theory, not independent validation. Count the 2x110 F_SE values and nuclear radii as external theory inputs.
Before unification, wrap Track A's relativity.F_SE/F_U so Z > 110 does not crash. Otherwise the unified predict() fails for (120,2) and similar inputs.

For neutral and near-neutral atoms, the best first-principles reference is LSDA Delta-SCF: 3.3% MAPE, MAE 0.29 eV, Z <= 54 only. GSHM gives 7.6% / 0.57 eV. A residual model on top of DFT would need DFT for all rows, which is too slow for this time box.

Literature position. Slater (1930) and Clementi-Raimondi (1963) are empirical screening rules; both are reproduced as baselines. Layzer (1959) is the 1/Z expansion with complex degeneracy, which Track A's exact dE1 and Layzer-complex treatment re-implement correctly. Edlén's isoelectronic formulas expand in zeta = q+1 with 1/(zeta + s) terms; GSHM's tau/(Za+kappa) is of this type. Screened-hydrogenic models with fitted l-split screening constants and relativistic corrections already exist: Mayer 1947; More 1982 (JQSRT); Faussurier, Blancard & Decoster 1997 (JQSRT 58, 233). They are typically good to a few % for ions. Delta-SCF LDA first IEs are known to be accurate to roughly 0.2-0.5 eV. Track A's 0.29 eV MAE matches that.

What appears genuinely new: (i) one global 30-32 parameter closed formula fitted and held-out-validated on all 5847 NIST IEs (Z = 1-110, all charge states) at about 1.6% MAPE, with a single universal Edlén-type kappa = 8.2; (ii) a complete table of exact first-order screening constants sigma1(N) for N = 1-110 compared with Slater's rules. Neither is a new physical law. Present them as a systematic, validated synthesis.
Quote one Bohr baseline in the unified doc (se_bohr 1362.9% ~ brief's 1365%). fp_bohr (1340%) handles rearranged rows differently.

Superheavy sanity check for the unified predict(): GSHM gives Og 6.59 eV against about 8.9 eV from the literature (roughly 26% low) and element 120 at 5.39 eV against about 5.8 eV. Label predictions for Z > 110 as qualitative.
